all_quotes.quote: Another mechanism considered was the neutral-radical reaction with the hydroxyl radical (OH); however, this reaction is too slow at $\sim$200 K to account for the observed patterns (see Section S4 of the Supporting Information).
Unfortunately, we do not have sufficient transitions in our data to test this hypothesis directly.

As stated previously, the observations presented here do not have sufficient lines available to test the spatial correlation of site-specific deuterated isotopologues, and dedicated high angular resolution observations targeting low-energy lines are necessary to further address this issue.
In the absence of directly analogous temperature-programmed desorption measurements of and themselves, we fit the curve of (cite: Souda2003) (Figure 3b, dotted line) between 110 K and 145 K.

As seen in Figure [\[fig:nvt\]](#fig:nvt)a, the desorption model based on work by (cite: Faure2015dhexchange) (dashed line) matches nicely the column density rise between 100 and 110 K; however, the in our data increases at temperatures up to $\sim$125 K.
